question: An item marked at ₹38,800 is available at a single discount of 25% or at two successive discounts of 10% and 15%. What will be the difference between the selling prices under these discount schemes?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

When the sum of two successive discounts (10% + 15%) is equal to the single discount (25%), the difference in the effective discount is directly given by (x × y) ÷ 100.

Difference in discount % = (10 × 15) ÷ 100 = 1.5%

The difference in Selling Price is simply this percentage applied to the Marked Price.

Difference = 1.5% of ₹38,800 = 1.5 × 388 = ₹582

**∴ The correct answer is ₹582.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Marked Price (MP) = ₹38,800

Discount Scheme 1 = 25% single discount

Discount Scheme 2 = 10% and 15% successive discounts

**Formula Used:**

Effective Successive Discount = x + y − (x × y) ÷ 100

Discount Value = MP × Discount %

 
 MP
 ₹38,800

 ₹29,100

 ₹29,682
 
 

 
 Diff: ₹582
 
 
 
 

 
 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Equivalent single discount for 10% and 15% = 10 + 15 − (10 × 15) ÷ 100

⇒ Effective discount = 25 − 1.5 = 23.5%

⇒ Difference in discount percentages = 25% − 23.5% = 1.5%

⇒ The difference in Selling Price is equivalent to the difference in the discount amounts.

⇒ Difference in Selling Price = 1.5% of ₹38,800

⇒ SP Difference = (1.5 ÷ 100) × 38,800 = 1.5 × 388 = ₹582

**∴ The correct answer is ₹582.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Successive Discount Formula

When two discounts of x% and y% are given successively, the equivalent single discount is given by: D = [x + y − (x × y) ÷ 100]%.

Marked Price (MP) and Selling Price (SP)

The selling price is calculated after deducting the discount from the marked price: SP = MP × (100 − Discount%) ÷ 100.

Buy X Get Y Free Concept

In promotional offers, the effective discount percentage is determined by: Discount % = [Free Items ÷ Total Items] × 100.
